name: Velsin Baobab-Ginger Tonic
description: A mid-market tonic water built around synth-baobab extract and real ginger oil, positioned as a 'digestive aid' to justify its slight premium. Comes in tall glass bottles with a matte earth-tone label.
flavor_profile: Earthy, faintly tart baobab with a sharp ginger bite and a mineral quinine finish — dry and complex
cultural_context: Popular in Tier 2 wellness circles and among augmented workers who believe the ginger oil interacts positively with certain neural implants — a claim Velsin neither confirms nor denies on its packaging.
story_hooks: A batch of Velsin tonic has been quietly recalled by Cadrex after reports of interference with older-model BCI implants — but the recall notice was buried in a compliance database almost no one reads.
Street chemists on the Shelf have started using Velsin tonic as a mixing agent for unlicensed compounds, and the flavor profile makes it nearly undetectable.
A Tier 3 bartender swears a specific combination of Velsin tonic and a black-market spirit cures a rare post-augmentation syndrome — and desperate people are starting to find her.
